sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year, from $23,693.0m in FY2016 to $51,824.0m in FY2025 [F168][F1][F10].
Revenue fell 58.0% to $13,662.0m in FY2020 [D161][F5], and the passages supplied do not explain that drop.
Revenue rose 76.5% to $61,049.0m in FY2022 [D238][F7], mainly on higher realized prices and volumes from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 [D274], primarily from lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
On the segment basis, Lower 48 added 8.0pp of FY2025 growth and now makes up 70.2% of revenue [D713][D711].
Total revenue rose 4.9% to $51,824.0m, driven by higher volumes including Marathon Oil, partly offset by lower realized crude prices [D342][F10][P28].
Crude oil is 66.3% of revenue [D551] but grew only 0.1% in FY2025 [D552].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6%, faster than revenue's 4.9%, so income before taxes fell to $12,656.0m from $13,672.0m [D352][D342][X91][X90].
Net income fell 13.6% and basic EPS fell 18.7%, while diluted shares rose 6.1% [D343][D344][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025 [F30], below the 17.9% window median [D831] and the 30.6% FY2022 high [D830].
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue from 36.6% [D326][D292], and D&A rose to 19.5% from 17.5% [D330][D296].
DD&A rose from $9,599.0m to $11,500.0m, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production [X60][X61][P22].
Production and operating expenses rose mainly from Marathon Oil and restructuring severance costs [P24].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, and net margin fell 3.3pp [D332][D298][D351]; no passage explains the tax move.
Operating cash flow of $19,796.0m was 2.48x net income of $7,988.0m [F59][D333][F20].
Operating cash flow fell 1.6% on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [D346][P6].
Capex was 1.35x D&A in FY2022 [D228], the last year the pack carries capex, so FY2025 free cash flow cannot be computed here.
Operating cash flow tracks commodity prices closely, so conversion should be judged across a cycle rather than one year [P4].
Net cash was $7,109.0m in FY2025, 12.1% of revenue, up from $6,134.0m [D337][D338][D303].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of six energy peers, against a peer median of -7.7% [D850][D851].
Buybacks of $5,018.0m and dividends of $3,995.0m totalled $9,013.0m, 46% of operating cash flow [X141][X151][D339][P31].
Diluted shares rose 6.1% to 1,253.4m, and the passages supplied do not explain the increase [D356][X131].
Table revenue differs from the as-reported figure in every year, so table growth rates compare one basis only; FY2025 as reported is $58,944.0m [F10][X10].
Net income fell 57.2% from $18,680.0m in FY2022 to $7,988.0m, a three-year CAGR of -24.7% [F17][F20][D845].
Lower revenues from lower commodity prices reduced FY2025 earnings [P12].
The $10.0 billion of unproved property [P2] is an impairment exposure if drilling disappoints; FY2025 impairments were only $26.0m [X121].
Net margin below the latest 15.4% [F30] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the decline; a return above the 17.9% median [D831] would reverse it.
Operating cash flow below $19,796.0m [F59] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the price-driven decline [P6].
Diluted shares above 1,253.4m [X131] in the FY2026 10-K would show buybacks not offsetting issuance.
